newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt to insist on rejected savings plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt to insist on rejected savings plan.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday that it would return retirement savings account legislation to the Senate for a second vote after the measure was blocked in the upper house of parliament on Tuesday night.
"We're still committed to RSAs, so you can probably draw from that that we will be doing it," a spokesman for Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp told Reuters.
The Labor Opposition joined with the minor Australian Democrats and Greens parties and independent Brian Harradine on Tuesday night to prevent the legislation from becoming law.
Under the legislation, banks and insurance companies would be able to offer Retirement Savings Accounts as an alternative to superannuation (pensions).
The spokesman said the accounts were a niche product aimed at low-income and itinerant workers and at workers with more than one job.
The Opposition and the Democrats said they objected to the legislation because the proposed accounts' rate of return was significantly lower than that of the superannuation funds.
But the spokesman said returns on the accounts would be low because their fees would be too.

"It just makes it easier for them. It's a low-fee, low-return product," he said. He would not comment on whether the government would now consider the Opposition's amendments, which were all defeated on Tuesday.
"I can't comment on what our thinking on that is at the moment," he said.
If the Senate rejects a House of Representatives bill and then rejects it again at least three months later, the government can dissolve the upper house -- the key to holding an early election.
